item.title: WPL to get more teams from next year? BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia shares latest update
item.description: NEW DELHI: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) is considering increasing the number of teams in the Women’s Premier League (WPL) from next year to provide more opportunities for women cricketers. BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia said the board will discuss the expansion after many players missed out on selection in the WPL 2027 auction held in Kochi. The league started in 2023 with five teams, and the 2027 season is scheduled to take place from January 14 to February 7. BCCI plans to expand WPL Saikia pointed out that the number of available players is much higher than the opportunities offered by the five existing teams. “There are about 150 players who are in the fray here and hardly 27 we had to take but still so many players were left out. So we can very easily see that five number of teams are really less compared to the number of supply chain of girls cricketers," Saikia said, as quoted by news agency IANS. “From next year, definitely we will have to do some brainstorming sessions to increase the number of teams as well as in other areas where we can improve. Not only the players but so many other areas we are having involvement in, right from the coaches, selectors, etc, and various stakeholders are involved here." Adding one or two teams and increasing player budgets could help more domestic players get a chance to compete at the highest level. “So the overall ecosystem has a positive impact on WPL. This is a wonderful beginning, and this is a wonderful journey going on and I hope WPL will grow from leaps and bounds in the coming years,” added Saikia. WPL's role in women's cricket Saikia also praised Delhi Capitals for signing 15-year-old uncapped all-rounder Uma Kashvi for Rs 10 lakh, calling it a positive step for young talent. “I am very happy that a young girl of 15 years got an opportunity to play in the WPL. That is a success. We want to bring maximum women cricketers to play and be a part of this success story in Indian women’s cricket.” He also credited the WPL for helping India become a stronger force in women’s cricket, highlighting the national team’s ODI World Cup victory last year. “We are the present champions in the world and that shows the expansion this WPL has given all across the country so far as women’s cricket is concerned. You see WPL is one of the big leagues in the world of franchise cricket after the IPL.” Saikia said the league has played an important role in India’s progress and expressed hope that it would continue to grow in the coming years.

item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Dylan Larkin was not at Tuesday’s game-day skate for the Detroit Red Wings. Soon, it appears he may no longer be skating with the Red Wings at all. There is plenty of scuttlebutt in NHL circles that a Larkin trade is about to go down. It’s the second straight day that Larkin has been absent. He missed Wednesday’s practice. Afterward, Detroit coach Todd McLellan described it as a maintenance day. Maybe Larkin just needed time to pack. That’s the reason why Larkin is being held out of workouts. McLellan did confirm to reporters on Thursday morning that Larkin would not be in the lineup in tonight’s game against the Chicago Blackhawks . “ Dylan Larkin won’t play in tonight’s game,” McLellan told reporters. Asked if Larkin was injured, McLellan added that Red Wings interim GM Shawn Horcoff would address the situation later in the day. item.title: Willson Contreras Addresses Playoff Comments, Sends Reassuring Message to Red Sox Fans
item.description: Willson Contreras Addresses Playoff Comments, Sends Reassuring Message to Red Sox Fans originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Red Sox 's season featured a stunning turnaround and playoff appearance, but it ended in disappointing fashion. They fell to the Yankees in the wild-card round, scoring just two runs across two games against their AL East rival. After falling to New York in Game 2, Willson Contreras expressed frustration with Boston's approach. "It's not enough when you have talent, or you have data, or you have computers that are telling you what to do. This is baseball," Contreras said . "The data is here to help us, but at the end of the day, you're gonna need experience and veteran guys to win games." Red Sox fans became concerned about the status of the relationship between Contreras and the organization, but the All-Star first baseman has made it clear that both sides are on "the same page." Contreras had a productive conversation with chief baseball officer Craig Breslow and manager Chad Tracy after Boston was eliminated. "After you lose in the playoffs and get kicked out, you get frustrated," Contreras told The Boston Globe's Peter Abraham . "But it was nothing to take personal. I think we had a great meeting. It's going to be good for next year. We're on the same page, which is the most important thing." Contreras added that "things are in a good place," and he is feeling much better physically after dealing with hamstring and hand injuries during the season. Contreras, who led the Red Sox with a career-high 27 home runs and 81 RBIs, is signed through the 2027 season. His deal includes a club option for the 2028 campaign. item.title: Jonah Coleman And Jeremiyah Love Headline The Week 8 Fantasy Football Rookie Stock Watch
item.description: Denver Broncos fullback Jonah Coleman (20) following the preseason game against the Green Bay Packers at Empower Field at Mile High. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The 2026 NFL rookie class has now played almost half a season, and their first season in the league is beginning to take shape. Some rookies have exceeded our expectations, while others have fallen well short. This is our fantasy football rookie stock watch heading into Week 8. Stock Up RB Jonah Coleman, Denver Broncos Leading up to the start of the season, we were adamant that Coleman would take over the starting job in Denver at some point this season. We may have seen that transition begin in Week 7 when Coleman returned from injured reserve. Coleman led the Broncos' backfield, playing on 49% of the team's offensive snaps and carrying the ball nine times. JK Dobbins took a back seat, playing on just 23% of snaps and rushing six times. The rookie was also much more efficient, averaging 6.0 yards per carry to Dobbins' 3.8 yards per carry. We expect Coleman's role to continue to grow moving forward. WR Caleb Douglas, Miami Dolphins Douglas entered the season as the Dolphins' WR1 and caught five passes for 94 yards in Week 1, before injuring his ankle in Week 2. He returned in Week 7 and went off for 70 yards and two touchdowns. It looks like he will continue to serve as the WR1 in Miami moving forward and could develop into a weekly starter. In his two full games, he has now caught seven of 10 targets for 164 yards and two touchdowns. Stock Down RB Jeremiyah Love, Arizona Cardinals Love's upside coming into the season was that of an elite RB1. That has gone out the window. While there is some hope that he could return and be a league winner, he has to get healthy first. He has now missed two games with an ankle injury and could miss a third this week. In five games this season, he rushed for 245 yards and one touchdown, while tacking on 36 yards and a touchdown through the air. This has been a disappointing rookie campaign for Love, to say the least, and we don't know when or if it will get better. RB Jadarian Price, Seattle Seahawks This is beginning to look like a bit of a lost season for Price. The first-round pick wasn't overly productive before going on injured reserve before Week 5, racking up just 119 yards on 28 carries and four receptions for 21 yards without scoring a single touchdown. Now, Zach Charbonnet is set to return and re-establish himself in the Seahawks' offense while Price remains on IR. Fantasy owners drafted him hoping he would give them RB1 upside. Now, once he returns, fantasy owners would be happy if he could just score his first NFL touchdown or give them a flex-worthy start. item.title: Happy Birthday Jesse Barfield and R.A. Dickey
item.description: CANADA - MARCH 01: Unlike previous Blue Jay spring camps, this one was much more relaxed, as demonstrated by right fielder Jesse Barfield below left, who turns the tables on news photographers. (Photo by Bernard Weil/Toronto Star via Getty Images) | Toronto Star via Getty Images Celebrating Jesse Barfield’s 67th Birthday Jesse Barfield has always been one of my favorite players. Barfield was selected in the 9th round of the 1977 amateur draft, the inaugural year for the Blue Jays and Mariners. MLB granted them the final two picks of each round, showcasing their generosity. Barfield debuted in the majors in 1981 and spent nine seasons with the Blue Jays. He ranks near the top of several franchise leaderboards: 4th in bWAR among position players, 29.5 2nd in defensive WAR, 9.5 (behind Tony Fernandez) 11th in slugging average, .483 11th in games played, 1032 7th in home runs, 179 9th in RBI, 527 Barfield was known for his powerful bat and exceptional defense, especially his strong, accurate arm in right field and remarkable range. Some even believed he could have excelled as a center fielder. There are countless legendary stories about his arm—like throwing a ball over the center-field fence from home plate. I remember watching him snare a line drive on a bounce and fire to first for the out. Barfield led the American League in outfield assists for three straight years (1985–87), largely because teams rarely risked running on his arm. In 1985 alone, he had eight outfield double plays, and from 1985–1987, he recorded 21—more than many teams tally in an entire season. Barfield, Lloyd Moseby, and George Bell formed an outfield trio that remains the best in Blue Jays history. During his time in Toronto, Barfield won two Gold Gloves, one Silver Slugger, and earned an All-Star selection. Many people contributed to my love of baseball, but the outfield of Bell, Moseby, and Barfield stands out. Watching them develop into the best outfield in baseball deepened my appreciation for the game. I often compared them to other legendary outfields—while not the greatest ever (the Tigers’ trio of Ty Cobb, Sam Crawford, and Bobby Veach likely holds that honor), I believe Bell, Moseby, and Barfield deserve a spot among the top ten outfields of all time. In 1989, the Blue Jays traded Barfield to the Yankees for Al Leiter—a heartbreaking deal that ultimately did not work out in Toronto’s favor. I once received a signed ball from Barfield in Cooperstown during Roy Halladay’s induction. Remarkably, he looked just as he did during his playing days. He was very friendly, but the thing i noticed most was his hands were twice the size of mine. Barfield remains active on social media: @JesseBarfield29. Happy birthday, Jesse! Wishing you a wonderful day. Celebrating R.A. Dickey’s 52nd Birthday R.A. Dickey joined the Blue Jays via trade from the Mets, along with catchers Mike Nickeas and Josh Thole. item.title: Carrick insists he is not surprised to still be in charge of Man Utd
item.description: Carrick insists he is not surprised to still be in charge of Man Utd Michael Carrick insists he does not need any assurances over his future as Manchester United manager despite growing criticism ahead of Saturday’s clash with Chelsea. United have endured a poor start to the season, leading to speculation around Carrick’s position. But the United boss says he has not sought any assurances over his future at the club. “I don’t need any assurances from anyone,” he said. “I totally get the position and understand the responsibilities, understand what comes with that, so I really don’t need any assurances from anyone in that regard. “I don’t see it really. I see the things that I need to see. I don’t look for it, it doesn’t really help in any way. “I care about what the supporters think, about what it feels like in the stadium and for travelling to games to come and see us, support us. “I care about what we give them and offer them and what they see. “I genuinely don’t take any notice of anything else. I know this job, I know what it brings and what we need to do to be better. I don’t need anyone else to tell me anything else.” Carrick also played down any suggestion of an issue with Bruno Fernandes after the midfielder did not feature against Bournemouth, following comments he made following the defeat to Como in which he questioned the team’s tactics. “It was a decision for what we felt for the game. That’s it,” he said. “Bruno is fully committed to this football club and there’s absolutely no issues with that. “We move forward, we make decisions as we go and we’re looking forward to the game on Saturday now.” Asked whether he was surprised to still be in charge, Carrick added: “No. “I’m here to do my job and the best for the team and I’m desperate to make us better and improve things. “I’m not surprised, no.” Stay up to date with all the latest Manchester United news by joining our Man Utd WhatsApp channel .

item.description: It is no secret that UFC fighters are rarely 100% healthy when they step into the Octagon. A few niggles, strains, or hidden injuries are part of the game. However, competing in a title fight at 38 while battling an illness and still putting on a dominant performance is something else entirely. That is exactly what Alexander Volkanovski did at UFC 333 . The Australian defeated previously undefeated Movsar Evloev via a second-round finish to defend his featherweight title. But what made the victory even more impressive was what Volk had been dealing with in the days leading up to the fight. The 38-year-old was battling a head cold, flu symptoms, and a chest infection during fight week in Abu Dhabi. He reportedly had a croaky voice, heavy breathing, and chest congestion. Things got so bad that his coach and several other members of his camp, who were staying in the same villa, also fell ill. Despite all that, Volk refused to take medication , believing it could give him an advantage over Evloev. While many fans were shocked by his decision to fight through the illness, his fellow Aussie Cody Thicknesse wasn’t surprised. According to the UFC fighter, a bout of flu was nothing compared to what the 145lbs champion had endured before previous fights. item.title: What will the weather be like for the Brewers parade and celebration?
item.description: The streets of downtown Milwaukee will be abuzz on the morning of Friday, Oct. 30 for the championship parade celebrating the Milwaukee Brewers ' long-awaited World Series win, but the weather will (thankfully) be uneventful. According to the National Weather Service, fans headed downtown for the 10 a.m. parade can expect cool temperatures but little threat of rain during the revelry. What weather is expected for the Brewers World Series parade? Temperatures are expected to hover around 50 degrees, a temperature peak for the day, when the parade begins, with a mix of sun and clouds expected throughout the morning, National Weather Service meteorologist Cameron Miller said on Oct. 29. Winds are also expected to be light, generally between 6 and 10 mph. Overcast conditions are expected to move in during the afternoon, but rain is not expected in the morning or early afternoon, Miller said. Buy Brewers World Series merchandise When and where is the parade? The World Series parade will take place Friday, Oct. 30 at 10 a.m., according to the Brewers. It will begin at the intersection of North 4th Street and West Wisconsin Avenue and proceed through downtown Milwaukee. The parade will end at Henry Maier Festival Park near the lakefront, where a rally will take place on the same grounds as Summerfest. The grounds will open at 8 a.m., and the first 50,000 fans at the rally will receive a limited-edition championship rally towel. What to expect at the rally: The rally will also include speeches in the American Family Insurance Amphitheater. Fans can purchase exclusive Brewers Parade/Rally merchandise, available only during the Championship Celebration at Henry Maier Festival Park. Admission to the Henry Maier Festival Park grounds is free for all fans until capacity is reached. But the Brewers are selling tickets to the American Family Insurance Amphitheater for rally speeches. Tickets go on sale Thursday, Oct. 29 starting at 10 a.m. for season ticket holders and 2 p.m. for everyone else. Screens showing the parade and rally will be scattered throughout the Summerfest grounds for fans without tickets to the amphitheater. Contact Claudia Levens at clevens@usatodayco.com. item.title: The Bears’ trade for Jeffery Simmons made NFL history
item.description: Tennessee Titans defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons (98) storms the field before the game against the Cleveland Browns at Nissan Stadium in Nashville, Tenn., Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. The NFL trade deadline isn’t until Nov. 10, but the action has been fast and furious this week, with multiple star players being moved. Defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons is the latest to change teams. On Thursday morning, the Chicago Bears acquired the 29-year-old Simmons from the Tennessee Titans in exchange for 2027 and 2028 first-round picks and a 2027 fourth-rounder. Tennessee also threw in a 2028 fifth-round pick along with the All-Pro defensive lineman. Not only did this deal establish the Bears as “all in” for the 2026 season, it made NFL history. A new price to pay ESPN’s Adam Schefter notes that this marks the first time in the common draft era (1967-present) that a defensive tackle was traded for two first-round picks. A first, literally: Jeffery Simmons is the first defensive tackle in the common draft era since 1967 to be traded for multiple first-round picks. https://t.co/EOrDCK5MCl — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) October 29, 2026 Premier defensive tackles getting moved for one first-round pick is fairly common. The Cincinnati Bengals traded the No. 10 overall pick, straight up, to the New York Giants for Dexter Lawrence last offseason, while the Dallas Cowboys included their 2027 first-rounder in last year’s deal with the New York Jets for Quinnen Williams. Simmons may be worth it Simmons’ price is unique, but so is he. Regarded by many as the finest defensive tackle in the NFL, the eight-year veteran is coming off a career-high 11 sacks and 17 tackles for loss in 2025. Through seven games this season, Simmons has posted 38 total tackles and four sacks. His 27 percent Pass Rush Win Rate as a defensive tackle is best in the NFL for 2026, according to ESPN . item.title: Women’s Sports Bars Scramble To Open Early For WNBA Finals Schedule
item.description: Game Four of the WNBA finals between the Golden State Valkyries and the Atlanta Dream on October 24th, 2026 at State Farm Arena in Atlanta Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The weekend is starting extra early for some sports fans this week. Tip-off for game six of the WNBA finals, a deciding match-up between the Golden State Valkyries (3-2) and Atlanta Dream (2-3), will take place at 12:30 p.m. ET at State Farm Arena in Atlanta. Professional sports championships rarely, if ever, are scheduled during weekday daytime slots. The lack of prime time programming left fans and sports-focused venues confused and frustrated when the schedule was announced on Monday, October 26. The game has since sold out. “I was pretty shocked,” says Nora McConnell-Johnson, owner of Babe’s Sports Bar in Chicago’s Logan Square neighborhood. McConnell-Johnson learned about the schedule for game six via a Slack channel she’s on with other owners of women’s sports bars. “We were all both immediately outraged and trying to figure out how to adjust to the new schedule. We’re all small businesses with small teams whose schedules have already been set for the week so this is a huge burden on all of us to figure out.” Let's Go Dream t-shirts on the seats before game six of the 2026 WNBA Finals between the Golden State Valkyries and the Atlanta Dream at State Farm Arena on October 29, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia Getty Images On weekdays, Babe’s typically opens at 4 p.m., but McConnell-Johnson knew she’d figure out a way to show the extraordinarily early finals games. "This has huge business implications, last year the WNBA finals were some of our highest sales days," she says. “The games this year are scheduled in a way that fans need to rearrange their calendars to catch them. The demand is there, but the access is not.” Babe’s is expecting thousands of dollars less in revenue this year due to the poor schedule. If the finals progress to game 7 on Saturday, October 31, Halloween will also create a challenge for venues to compete with holiday celebrations. By Tuesday, it became clear that the WNBA schedule would not be changing despite plenty of criticism. Rikki’s , a women’s sports bar in San Francisco, announced an 8:30 a.m. PT opening for Thursdays’ game, with a pop-up breakfast menu and drink specials. Level Sporting Club, another women’s sports bar in Chicago, started promoting a “Work from Level” game day experience with reservations available to book a remote work station to cheer, eat brunch, and take advantage of the bar’s Wifi on a work day. In New York, Wilka’s, a women’s sports bar on the Lower East Side, announced a 9 a.m. opening with coffee and pastries, plus breakfast until 11:30 a.m., plus wifi for workers. In Brooklyn, Blazers is offering a Work from Blazers early opening. Nearby, Athena Keke’s opens daily at 9 a.m., but nearly every women’s sports bar in the country had to rearranged their schedule, staffing, and ordering to accommodate the unusual finals schedule.

item.title: WNBA Finals ticket prices plummet ahead of Game 6
item.description: Oct 26, 2026; San Francisco, California, USA; Golden State Valkyries guard Tiffany Hayes (15) celebrates after scoring as Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese (5) looks on in the third quarter of game five of the 2026 WNBA Finals at Chase Center. Mandatory Credit: David Gonzales-Imagn Images The Atlanta Dream are facing elimination in Game 6 of the WNBA Finals on Thursday, but fans hoping to catch the game in person can get in for a bargain as ticket prices have plummeted leading up to the game. The collapse in prices came after the WNBA moved Game 6 from primetime to a 12:30 p.m. ET tipoff on a weekday. According to one ticketing expert, resellers who bought up tickets may have badly misjudged the demand for an afternoon game. Game 6 Moved to the Afternoon The Dream took a 2-1 lead in the series before dropping back-to-back games to the Golden State Valkyries, who now have a chance to clinch the championship in Atlanta. Earlier this week, the league moved Game 6 from 8 p.m. to 12:30 p.m. on Thursday because of a Hawks game that night. The change allowed the Dream to play at the 17,000-seat State Farm Arena rather than the 3,500-seat Gateway Center, where they played their regular-season games, according to Front Office Sports . The Dream also sold out Games 3 and 4, and a team spokesperson told Front Office Sports that Game 6 had sold out, leaving only tickets on the secondary market. Prices Collapse The get-in price for Game 6 was $32 on the resale market as of Wednesday morning, according to TicketData. For comparison, the get-in price was $166 for Game 3 and $246 for Game 4. Prices dipped even lower in some places. The get-in price on TickPick dropped from $156 on Monday to as low as $23 on Wednesday, according to NBA Central . TicketData founder Keith Pagello said that resellers likely got burned by a number of factors. “It seems like they were either banking on the Dream winning Game 5 and setting up a chance to celebrate a championship at home, or simply underestimated how much demand would be muted by a noon start on a weekday,” Pagello told Front Office Sports. The average resale price was about $105 on Monday night, even after Atlanta lost Game 5, before it began to collapse on Tuesday morning. Prices had ticked back up slightly by Thursday morning, with the get-in price sitting at $38, per Front Office Sports . Obviously, a midday tipoff on a Thursday isn’t ideal for many fans. But for anyone who can get out of work, it’s a chance to watch a potential title-clinching game for less than the price of most regular-season tickets. item.title: Fedor Emelianenko bats down ‘nonsense’ narrative from UFC boss Dana White — ‘He always changes his story’
item.description: Dana White’s biggest regret, at least back in 2013 , was never signing former PRIDE FC Heavyweight Champion Fedor Emelianenko , who went on to compete f or Strikeforce and Bellator MMA under fighter-friendly promoter and new Ki MMA head cheese Scott Coker. Promoters don’t typically regret signing “overrated” fighters who get knocked out by smaller opponents , though it’s hard to gauge authenticity when it comes to White’s hyperbole. “There are different kinds of businessmen, some are decent and respectful, some people don’t even need a contract,” Emelianenko told Ushatayka (transcribed by Bloody Elbow ). “A handshake is enough to keep their word. But now, Dana is talking all sorts of nonsense. First he wanted me, then he didn’t. The he regretted it, then he’s glad he never signed me. The man talks and always changes his story. He simply doesn’t stand by his words. His way of doing business doesn’t sit well with me.” It also doesn’t sit well with Vadummy , the promoter for M-Done . “I didn’t understand the point of his actions,” Emelianenko (40-7, 1 NC) added. “He came over saying, ‘I want you to fight for me,’ he made that very clear. But one fight earlier, I’d been a free agent. I was free and they didn’t sign me. It happened every time. When I’m free they aren’t interested, when I’m under contract, the offers start coming. But if you’re under contract you can’t sign another one. There would be legal proceedings.” UFC is something of an expert on heavyweight legal proceedings . White and Co. never got the Brock Lesnar super fight they were hoping for , but the 50-year-old Emelianenko did face his fair share of former UFC champions, knocking out Tim Sylvia , Frank Mir , Andrei Arlovski , and Rampage Jackson , just to name a few.
